toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The departures are concentrated in Kestrel, not the group generally or the firm. 8 of the 11 associates on Kestrel have resigned, against 1 of the 13 who never worked on it. Other groups' attrition is flat, which counts against the firm-wide hours increase and ordinary market mobility as the main explanation. Pay may play a part, but it doesn't explain why the loss sits almost entirely on one matter.

I can't yet separate the workload on Kestrel from Dorian Faulk's supervision. All 11 Kestrel associates report to him, and he supervises on no other matter. The survey points to both: weekend work and late-night, publicly copied corrections. The exit forms are uninformative. They are tick-box, leavers were told the group head might see them, and they record no matter or partner.

I'm fairly sure about where the problem sits. I'm not sure why. I wouldn't announce the £12k payment or close the review. It could miss the cause and cost £228k. Next, commission the independent confidential interviews, about £9k and three weeks. Design them to separate workload from supervision. Add matter and supervisor fields to attrition tracking. Hold the supervision change and the contract-reviewer decision until the interviews report. Kestrel's review phase runs to December, so the interviews need to move quickly.
